candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall handle and dispose of sewage sludge in accordance with Section 405 of the Clean Water Act and all other applicable Federal regulations to protect public health and the environment from any reasonably anticipated adverse effects due to any toxic pollutants which may be present in the sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which federal Section 405 and other applicable regulations impose enforceable pollutant limits beyond Table 1 could change which numeric limits are deemed applicable for land-applied sludge.

candidates.exact_span: If requirements for sludge management practices or pollutant criteria become more stringent than the sludge pollutant limits or acceptable management practices in this permit, or control a pollutant not listed in this permit, this permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform to the requirements promulgated at Section 405(d)(2) of the Clean Water Act.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether later Section 405(d)(2) criteria have superseded in-permit Table 1 limits or added pollutants not listed in the permit affects which enforceable limits apply (A) and which monitoring/management obligations govern (B).

candidates.exact_span: If new limits for Molybdenum are promulgated prior to permit expiration, then those limits shall become directly enforceable.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditional direct enforceability of Molybdenum limits depends on whether such limits were promulgated before permit expiration, which could add or change an applicable numeric limit not stated in this segment.

candidates.exact_span: These changes may justify the application of permit conditions that are different from or absent in the existing permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a planned change in sewage sludge disposal practice triggered different or additional permit conditions affects which limits and monitoring requirements are treated as applicable during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The one-time TCLP testing window tied to permit effective date determines whether TCLP monitoring was required, already due, or satisfied relative to Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required sampling point and timing for TCLP testing affects whether available measurements satisfy the monitoring obligation (B) and whether absent or mistimed results leave compliance or missing-evidence status unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 262.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A hazardous-waste determination shifts the regulatory regime from land-application Table 1 limits to RCRA disposal standards, changing applicable enforceable limits (A) and the monitoring/disposal obligations in force (B).

candidates.exact_span: The disposal of sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste, in other than a certified hazardous waste disposal facility shall be prohibited.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This prohibitory standard provides an enforceable compliance criterion distinct from Table 1 pollutant concentration limits when sludge is classified as hazardous waste.

candidates.exact_span: The Information Management Section, telephone no. (214) 665-6750, and the appropriate state agency shall be notified of test failure within 24 hours. A written rep ort shall be provided to this office within 7 days after failing the TCLP.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These reporting deadlines define post-failure monitoring/reporting obligations (B) and determine what documented evidence of TCLP failure or follow-up must exist to resolve missing-data cases (C).

candidates.exact_span: The report will contain test results, certification that unauthorized disposal has not occurred and a summary of alternative disposal plans that comply with RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Required report contents set the evidentiary standard for failed-TCLP situations; partial or absent reports may be classified differently as documented no-data, inadequate evidence, or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall not be applied to the land if the concentration of the pollutants exceeds the pollutant concentration criteria in Table 1.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This ties enforceable land-application compliance directly to Table 1 pollutant concentration criteria; interpretation of which pollutants and numeric thresholds Table 1 contains governs limit-exceedance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of testing for pollutants in Table 1 is found in Element 1, Section I.C.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Monitoring frequency for Table 1 pollutants is not specified in this segment and depends on Section I.C; without that cross-reference, whether Table 1 testing was required in FY2025 and how to treat missing results remains unresolved.
